Daily Brief

Americans head to the polls today in midterm elections that could reshape the balance of power in Congress, with Democrats seeking to capitalize on voter discontent over inflation and President Trump's eight-month war with Iran [Globe and Mail], [Al Jazeera], [RFI]. The conflict intensified overnight as the US conducted limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, described by officials as defensive responses to IRGC fire on American aircraft [BBC], [France 24]. Meanwhile, diplomatic efforts continue with the Kremlin confirming US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks will proceed in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 [The Hindu], offering a potential path toward ending the four-year conflict. In a significant development for post-Brexit trade, the UK and EU have reached a draft agreement to eliminate red tape on food exports, with officials claiming £5.1bn in annual economic benefits [BBC Europe]. The humanitarian toll of ongoing conflicts remains stark: Russian bombing killed 29 people at a Ukrainian aid distribution center in Zaporizhzhia [BBC Europe], while Africa's unprecedented Ebola outbreak has reached 10,000 cases with nearly 5,000 deaths, prompting warnings it could spread globally [The Guardian].

01 Conflict

US Conducts Strikes on Iranian Island as Midterm Elections Begin

  • US forces struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with officials describing the action as limited and defensive in response to IRGC firing on a US aircraft
  • Iran's IRGC claimed to have shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and one MQ-9 drone east of the strait
  • Trump told reporters he was in 'no rush' to escalate strikes, noting Iran had been 'crippled financially,' while suggesting the US 'might need to go after' Iran's underground nuclear site at Pickaxe Mountain
  • Brent crude rose 1.7% to $106.58 per barrel following reports of the strikes

Millions Vote in US Midterm Elections Amid Economic Discontent and Iran War Fatigue

  • All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are being contested, with Democrats needing net gains of 3 House seats and 4 Senate seats for majorities
  • More than 57 million Americans cast early ballots, with heavy turnout in battleground states including Georgia, Michigan, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas

03 Geopolitics

Kremlin Confirms US-Mediated Russia-Ukraine Talks in Abu Dhabi Next Week

  • Russia confirmed trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US will take place November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi
  • Russian delegation will be led by Vladimir Medinsky, a Putin aide who participated in failed 2022 negotiations
  • US special envoy Steve Witkoff met with both Putin and Zelenskyy last month to arrange the talks
  • Medinsky, born in Ukraine, has co-authored Russian history textbooks praising Moscow's role in Ukraine

Russian Bombing Kills 29 at Ukrainian Aid Distribution Center

  • At least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs struck the village of Komyshuvakha in Zaporizhzhia region on Monday
  • 29 people confirmed dead including two rescuers and four police officers, with 48 reported missing
  • President Zelenskyy stated Russia targeted a school used for humanitarian aid distribution, with a second strike hitting the shelter location
  • The attack came as US-mediated peace talks were confirmed for the following week

05 Economics

UK and EU Reach Draft Agreement to Remove Post-Brexit Food Export Checks

  • A 200-page draft sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) agreement would eliminate health certificates and inspection fees for food exports
  • The deal would allow resumption of exports including fresh sausages, burgers, shellfish, and seed potatoes to the EU
  • UK government claims the agreement will deliver £5.1 billion in annual economic benefits
  • Draft texts for emissions trading and youth travel schemes were also circulated ahead of the UK-EU summit later this month
